comments.body:
Debian tests are failing with
```
Sep 02 23:18:22 lima-container-libs-ci kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 33129 (lockfile.test) total-vm:5175756kB, anon-rss:250744kB, file-rss:16kB, shmem-rss:6268kB, UID:0 pgtables:2424kB oom_score_adj:0
```

5 GB for a test is really excessive, but with anonymous only 250 MB, I’m not sure where that goes.

Cc: @timcoding1988 in case this rings a bell.

Considering this only fails on debian I wonder if this is a problem with the exact go version in debian? It was never a problem before, it does not fail on fedora either and I do not see how such a test can use that much memory.

A local run on my fedora system shows a lot less memory usage
```
$ /usr/bin/time -v ./lockfile.test 
PASS
        Command being timed: "./lockfile.test"
        User time (seconds): 0.47
        System time (seconds): 1.10
        Percent of CPU this job got: 1%
        Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 1:22.54
        Average shared text size (kbytes): 0
        Average unshared data size (kbytes): 0
        Average stack size (kbytes): 0
        Average total size (kbytes): 0
        Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 28764
        Average resident set size (kbytes): 0
        Major (requiring I/O) page faults: 0
        Minor (reclaiming a frame) page faults: 134495
        Voluntary context switches: 33968
        Involuntary context switches: 3004
        Swaps: 0
        File system inputs: 0
        File system outputs: 0
        Socket messages sent: 0
        Socket messages received: 0
        Signals delivered: 0
        Page size (bytes): 4096
        Exit status: 0
```

Mhh, actually looking at the error output is one of the child process which gets reliably killed not the parent test, hence the `signal: killed` log line in the tests which should be the cmd.Wait() error.

And then looking at the test runs they seem to use -race, they don't log the go test line in the Makefile (something we should do IMO) so not 100% sure. With race the thing is much much slower and I guess takes a lot more memory. Then add up to 150 plus child processes in parallel in TestLockfileMultiprocessMixed and things might get close memory wise so the OOM killer took action.

The problem is the rexec includes the race detector in the child which I guess make no sense, or rather we would not want the child to consume the extra memory that imposes?

debian ships go 1.27 now while fedora stable is at 1.26 so I guess the difference might be because of that?
